items.note: Experiment comparing human-only, human-AI collaboration, and AI-only design of CSR initiatives, with quality, novelty, and feasibility scored by experts and GenAI; the human-only versus collaboration arms are the relevant contrast, and assignment and sample size are not stated in the conference abstract.

CHI system paper (Creative Blends, LLM plus text-to-image) with a user study of 24 participants reporting more creative, metaphorically richer blend ideation; the abstract does not say whether there is a baseline condition or whether creativity is rated on outputs, and N is below 50 (same work as arXiv 2502.16062).

Study 2 has people generate ideas with a culturally aligned versus misaligned LLM (ChatGPT versus ErnieBot) and scores usefulness and novelty of ideas (an AI-configuration contrast); Study 1 is model-only and Study 3 uses field data; assignment and N not stated in the conference abstract.

CHI study with 52 novices comparing the DesignWeaver prompt-scaffolding interface for text-to-image product design with a baseline (one AI configuration versus another), reporting more diverse and innovative designs; design (between or within subjects) and assignment not stated (same work as arXiv 2502.09867).

Randomized study at ICLR 2025 giving LLM feedback to over 20,000 peer reviews; outcomes are review length, informativeness, and engagement, not creativity or diversity of a creative task (a reviewer may still want to confirm scope).

Mixed-method classroom experiments with AI-supported ideation in industrial and UI design education plus surveys, reporting higher creativity; the abstract does not describe a comparison group, how creativity is measured (possibly self-report), or the sample size.

Semantic feature generation task where participants can request algorithmically generated hints chosen by a bandit, versus the standard task, with number of features generated as the outcome (fluency); unclear whether the hints come from a generative model (GPT-4 appears as a simulated participant), so generative-AI scope needs checking.

Controlled user study in which design-engineering participants solved conceptual design challenges with GPT-4 without explanations (n=39) or with an XAI-enhanced LLM framework (n=39), and 10 raters scored usefulness, feasibility, originality, and credibility; 78 designers plus 10 raters (88 total), assignment not stated.

ICCC 2025 paper comparing improvised 'Yes! and' stories that people co-created with an LLM agent versus with a human partner, rated on novelty, value, and surprise (no difference); abstract from the ICCC 2025 program page, with no DOI, N, or assignment stated.

Between-subjects study with 46 participants on 2D structure design comparing a high-fidelity and a low-fidelity reflective LLM agent with a no-AI control; outcomes are engineering performance, solution quality (symmetry, alignment with optimal designs), and process measures rather than creativity ratings, and N is below 50.
